unit: Ch 9: Income Tax Liability: Computation and Optimisation
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Meaning of Total Income and Capacities of Earning
explain: Gross Total Income combines taxable profits from all five heads of income.
Clubbing rules and loss set-off provisions apply before arriving at Gross Total Income.
Deductions under Chapter VIII are subtracted from Gross Total Income to get Total Income.
Salary or interest received by a partner from an LLP or firm is taxed as business income.
A partner's share of firm profit is completely exempt from income tax.
Income from an impartible estate is taxed in the hands of the eldest member.

flow.title: Steps to Arrive at Total Income
steps: Aggregate income under all five heads

topics.example: A partner gets Rs. 50,000 salary and Rs. 2,00,000 profit share from a firm; only Rs. 50,000 is taxed as business income.
remember: Share of profit from a partnership firm is exempt under Schedule III Table Sl.No.2.
mistakes: Adding the partner's share of firm profit to their individual taxable income.

quiz.q: How is the share of profit received by a partner from a firm treated in the partner's hands?
o: Taxable under Income from Other Sources
quiz.why: A partner's share of profit in a firm is specifically exempt under Schedule III.

quiz.q: Salary and bonus received by a partner from an LLP are assessed under which head?
o: Profits and gains of business or profession
quiz.why: Remuneration to a partner is taxable as business income to the extent allowed as a deduction to the firm.

topics.title: Steps for Computation of Total Income and Tax Payable
explain: Follow a structured sequence from residential status determination to final tax payment.
Classify all earnings under the five designated heads of income.
Apply clubbing provisions and set-off or carry-forward rules for losses.
Deduct eligible Chapter VIII reliefs to obtain Total Income.
Round off both Total Income and net tax payable to the nearest multiple of Rs. 10.
Deduct prepaid taxes like TDS, TCS, and advance tax to find the final tax due or refund.

flow.title: Process of Final Tax Determination
steps: Subtract TDS, TCS, and advance tax

topics.example: If net tax liability computes to Rs. 44,408, it is rounded off to Rs. 44,410 before payment.
remember: Total income and net tax liability or refund must be rounded off to the nearest Rs. 10.
mistakes: Forgetting to round off the final tax payable or refundable to the nearest ten rupees.

quiz.q: To what multiple must total income and net tax liability be rounded off?
quiz.why: Total income and tax payable are required to be rounded off to the nearest multiple of Rs. 10.

quiz.q: Advance tax liability arises during the year if net tax payable after TDS/TCS is at least:
quiz.why: Advance tax is required to be paid if the estimated tax payable after TDS/TCS is Rs. 10,000 or more.

topics.title: Tax Rates under Default Regime vs Optional Regime
explain: The default tax regime under section 202(1) offers lower slab rates with a basic exemption of Rs. 4,00,000.
Slab rates progress in Rs. 4,00,000 steps at 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, and max out at 30% above Rs. 24,00,000.
Under the optional regime, basic exemption is Rs. 2,50,000 for non-seniors, Rs. 3,00,000 for senior citizens, and Rs. 5,00,000 for super seniors.
Optional regime slabs jump from 5% to 20% above Rs. 5,00,000, and 30% above Rs. 10,00,000.
Special tax rates apply to specific incomes like capital gains and lottery winnings under both regimes.
topics.example: Under default regime, income of Rs. 7,00,000 pays 5% on Rs. 3,00,000, which equals Rs. 15,000.
remember: Basic exemption limit under default regime is Rs. 4,00,000 for all individuals.
mistakes: Applying higher senior citizen basic exemption limits under the default tax regime.

quiz.q: What is the basic exemption limit under the default regime under section 202(1)?
quiz.why: Under section 202(1), the basic exemption limit for all individuals is Rs. 4,00,000.

quiz.q: Under the optional tax regime, what is the tax rate for income between Rs. 5,00,001 and Rs. 10,00,000?
quiz.why: The normal slab rates under the optional regime tax income between Rs. 5,00,001 and Rs. 10,00,000 at 20%.

topics.title: Surcharge, Marginal Relief, Rebate, and Cess
explain: Under default regime, surcharge caps at 25% for income exceeding Rs. 2 crore.
Under optional regime, surcharge can reach up to 37% for income exceeding Rs. 5 crore.
Surcharge on dividend and specific capital gains is capped at 15% under both regimes.
Rebate under section 156 gives up to Rs. 60,000 under default regime if total income is up to Rs. 12,00,000.
Rebate under optional regime is up to Rs. 12,50,000 for resident individuals with income up to Rs. 5,00,000.
Health and Education Cess is uniformly levied at 4% on the aggregate of income tax and surcharge.
topics.example: A resident individual with total income of Rs. 11,00,000 under default regime gets full rebate of their computed tax since it is below Rs. 60,000.
remember: Rebate under section 156 is available only to resident individuals.
mistakes: Allowing section 156 rebate to a non-resident individual.

quiz.q: What is the maximum surcharge rate under the default tax regime under section 202(1)?
quiz.why: The maximum surcharge rate under the default tax regime is capped at 25%.

quiz.q: Rebate under section 156 under the default regime is available up to a total income of:
quiz.why: Resident individuals with total income up to Rs. 12,00,000 can claim rebate up to Rs. 60,000 under section 202(1).

topics.title: Alternate Minimum Tax (AMT) and Tax Credit
explain: AMT ensures non-corporate taxpayers claiming specified deductions pay a baseline minimum tax.
AMT applies at 18.5% plus surcharge and cess on Adjusted Total Income.
It does not apply to individuals paying tax under the default regime under section 202(1).
It also does not apply if the individual's Adjusted Total Income does not exceed Rs. 20 lakh.
Adjusted Total Income adds back deductions claimed under section 46 and Chapter VIII Part C (except section 149).
Excess of AMT paid over regular tax creates an AMT credit that can be carried forward for up to 15 tax years.

flow.title: AMT Applicability and Credit Mechanism
steps: Check if assessee opted out of 202(1)
Check if Adjusted Income exceeds 20 lakhs
Compare AMT with regular income tax
Pay higher of regular tax or AMT
Carry forward excess AMT as credit

topics.example: If regular tax is Rs. 19,81,980 and AMT is Rs. 30,64,450, assessee pays Rs. 30,64,450 and carries forward Rs. 10,82,470 credit.
remember: AMT credit can be carried forward for a maximum of 15 tax years.
mistakes: Applying AMT provisions to an individual who is being taxed under the default regime.

quiz.q: What is the base rate of Alternate Minimum Tax (before surcharge and cess)?
quiz.why: AMT is calculated at the rate of 18.5% on Adjusted Total Income.

quiz.q: How long can unabsorbed AMT credit be carried forward?
quiz.why: AMT credit can be carried forward and set off for up to 15 succeeding tax years.

topics.title: Tax Planning and Salary Structuring
explain: Standard deduction is Rs. 75,000 under the default regime and Rs. 50,000 under the optional regime.
Allowances like HRA, Children Education Allowance, and LTC are exempt only if the employee opts out of default regime.
Under the default regime, interest on loan for a self-occupied house cannot be set off against other heads.
Employer contribution to RPF, NPS, and superannuation fund combined in excess of Rs. 7,50,000 is a taxable perquisite.
Non-business individuals can choose between default and optional regimes year after year.
Individuals with business income can opt out of default regime once, and if they switch back, cannot opt out again.

flow.title: Regime Selection for Salaried Individuals
steps: Compute salary net of Rs. 75,000 deduction
Evaluate available exemptions under optional regime
Compute total deductions under Chapter VIII
Compare net take-home and tax payable
Select the regime yielding lower net tax

topics.example: An employee eligible for Rs. 2,04,000 HRA exemption and Rs. 2,00,000 home loan interest benefits more by opting out of the default regime.
remember: Standard deduction for salary is Rs. 75,000 under default regime and Rs. 50,000 under optional regime.
mistakes: Claiming HRA or self-occupied house property interest loss under the default tax regime.

quiz.q: What is the standard deduction from salary available under the default regime under section 202(1)?
quiz.why: Standard deduction under section 19(1) for default regime is Rs. 75,000.

quiz.q: Can an individual having business income shift in and out of the default regime every year freely?
o: No, withdrawal of opt-out is allowed only once
Only with prior permission from CBDT
Never allowed to opt out at all
quiz.why: Assessees with business income can withdraw the option only once and thereafter cannot re-enter the optional regime.
